searchText: FYI March 18th meeting is labeled as feb 18th PRs welcome. 🙂 I’ve never done one I’ll see if I can figure it out Login to GitHub, navigate to the README.md file, click the little pencil in the top right. Make the correction, commit, create pull request. Kk Ty A bit easier from a computer than mobile, but it is possible to do via mobile as well. thanks these made it easy Do you usually edit the notes or leave them raw? For something as simple as this, I think what you put is plenty. For a more complex change I usually leave some reasoning/discussion as well. Oh I mean the dev meeting notes: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/blob/master/AllCoreDevs-Meetings/Meeting%20134.md An obvious example of a critical correction: "You know, early June around mid June June and July, we would probably have like 14-15 second block times, which is high, but not manageable and late July early August, assuming like things are the same, you probably are lucky he had like 17 or more and that's supposed to be. " I assume Tim meant to say manageable. <@!552133098075193354> would be the right person to ask if PRs to meeting notes would be valuable. My *guess* is it probably isn't worth fixing them up. FWIW, I (likely) said 14-15 sec is not *un*manageable Yeah I figured. One issue with the notes is that the meaning of things changes in a few places because of errors. Was wondering if the critical errors should be corrected I can submit a pr for the ones I saw but likely due to lack of technical knowledge I will miss some. I think if we wanted to deeply proofread them, we’d basically need to double the cost. Perhaps that’s worth considering, cc: <@!642887713246150666> This looks like a typo, because rest of the details on the Readme seems to be correct. I suppose, PR #503 was to update the Readme file till meeting ACD 134. Thanks for user (misher2 ) for making a new PR to fix the typo. PRs for ACD and CL meetings are usually available within 5 days of the meeting. Any correction in the period before it is merged, is highly appreciated. However, anyone can make a PR to update that later. In this case, I can follow up with the user (who documented the notes) to update it, if that's helpful. In my experience, documenting ACD and CL meetings are generally a little challenging for non-tech user (who document the notes) and they try their best to document with the help of captions and own ability to pick up the correct term. I would not rely 100 % on the notes, however happy to invite people who are willing to proof read and will also look into the cost part of documentation, if that's helpful. I think, one immediate measure that can be helpful could be adding time stamp in notes at places of confusion or important piece of information. So, people be able to follow the recording at the point in case of clarification. I will get this fixed ASAP. Kk I like the timestamp idea, at least for discussion topics, not necessarily every reply I often skim the videos myself looking for a topic when I want to make sure I’m explaining something right 😅
